quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #23
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: You see a green light, but traffic is blocking the intersection ahead. What should you do?

options.text: Turn left and find another route.
Wait outside the intersection until traffic clears.
Follow other vehicles into the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait outside the intersection until traffic clears.
questions.explanation: A green light does not mean you should enter the intersection if it is blocked. Do not enter if other vehicles are in your way. If you get stuck in the intersection when the light turns red, you will block cross traffic and may get a ticket.

questions.question: Where should you place your hands when using hand-to-hand steering?

options.text: Left hand at 9-10 o'clock, right hand at 2-3 o'clock
Left hand at 10-11 o'clock, right hand at 1-2 o'clock
Left hand at 7-8 o'clock, right hand at 4-5 o'clock

questions.correctAnswerText: Left hand at 7-8 o'clock, right hand at 4-5 o'clock
questions.explanation: Use hand-to-hand steering (also called push-pull steering) when driving normally at speeds above 15 mph. Think of the steering wheel as a clock face. Your left hand should be at 7-8 o'clock and your right hand at 4-5 o'clock.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: No right turn.
Drive only in the direction the arrow points.
Curve ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive only in the direction the arrow points.
questions.explanation: This is a regulatory sign. It tells drivers what they must do. When you see this sign, you must drive in the direction the arrow shows.

questions.question: A driver license is a:

options.text: Requirement.
Privilege.
Right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Privilege.
questions.explanation: Driving is a privilege, not a right. All drivers must keep roads safe. If you misuse this privilege, it can be taken away.

questions.question: When can you legally turn left at a red light after stopping?

options.text: When you turn from a two-way street onto a two-way street.
When you turn from a one-way street onto another one-way street.
When you yield to all other traffic at the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you turn from a one-way street onto another one-way street.
questions.explanation: After a complete stop, you can turn left at a red light only if you are on a one-way street and turning onto another one-way street. Make sure no signs forbid this turn.

questions.question: Why should you not use high beam headlights in fog or mist?

options.text: The light will bounce back into your eyes.
Oncoming vehicles might not see you.
Vehicles behind you may tailgate.

questions.correctAnswerText: The light will bounce back into your eyes.
questions.explanation: In fog or mist, do not use high beam headlights. The light will bounce back and shine into your eyes, making it harder to see.

questions.question: When entering the interstate, you check for a gap, match the traffic speed, and signal. What should you do next?

options.text: Expect other traffic to let you in because you have the right-of-way.
Merge carefully into the gap.
Wait for the lane to be completely clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Merge carefully into the gap.
questions.explanation: Find a gap in traffic, speed up to match other vehicles, and signal. Merge carefully into the gap when safe. Watch for other traffic and do not expect drivers to make room for you.

questions.question: Your view at an intersection is blocked. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down and look both ways.
Keep your speed and look both ways.
Stop, then inch forward until you can see both directions clearly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, then inch forward until you can see both directions clearly.
questions.explanation: Always slow down at intersections. If you cannot see cross traffic clearly, come to a complete stop. Then inch forward until you can see clearly in both directions.

questions.question: How should you avoid glare from an oncoming car's headlights?

options.text: Look briefly toward the right side of the road.
Keep your eyes on the center line of the road.
Flash your high beams.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look briefly toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Do not look at the bright lights of an oncoming vehicle. Instead, glance toward the right side of the road for a moment. Then look ahead again to track the position of the other car.

questions.question: Your vehicle's rear is skidding to the left. What should you do?

options.text: Do not turn your steering wheel.
Turn your steering wheel to the left.
Turn your steering wheel to the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your steering wheel to the left.
questions.explanation: If you skid on a wet or icy road, take your foot off the gas, do not brake, and steer in the direction of the skid. If your car has anti-lock brakes, press the brakes firmly and steer straight.

questions.question: If your car begins to skid out of control, what should you do?

options.text: Pump the brakes.
Apply the brakes lightly.
Do not use the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not use the brakes.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle skids, do not touch the brakes. Keep steering until your vehicle is under control and moving safely.

questions.question: What color are regulatory signs?

options.text: Green.
Yellow.
White.

questions.correctAnswerText: White.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs tell drivers about laws they must follow. These signs are usually white squares or rectangles with black, red, or green letters or symbols.

questions.question: What should you do if your vehicle is skidding?

options.text: Brake lightly.
Do not use the brakes.
Brake hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not use the brakes.
questions.explanation: Do not use the brakes when your vehicle is skidding. Braking can make the skid worse.

questions.question: When you see a flashing red light at an intersection, what must you do?

options.text: Stop completely, let traffic and pedestrians pass, then go.
Slow down and proceed with caution.
Stop and wait until the light turns green.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, let traffic and pedestrians pass, then go.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. Come to a complete stop, then go when it is safe.

questions.question: When parallel parking downhill, which way should you turn your wheels?

options.text: Turn them toward the curb or road edge.
Turn them away from the curb or road edge.
Keep them straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn them toward the curb or road edge.
questions.explanation: When parking downhill, turn your front wheels toward the curb or road edge. This helps prevent your car from rolling into traffic if the brakes fail.

questions.question: If another driver is passing you in a no passing zone, what should you do?

options.text: Pull off the road.
Keep the same speed and position.
Slow down to let them safely return to your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to let them safely return to your lane.
questions.explanation: Slow down to help the passing vehicle return to the lane safely. This helps avoid hazards ahead.

questions.question: If you have a sudden tire blowout while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Use the brakes lightly.
Pump the brakes.
Brake hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the brakes lightly.
questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel tightly and keep driving straight. Slow down gradually by releasing the gas pedal and using the brakes lightly.

questions.question: What does this red and white sign mean?

options.text: Stop and look both ways before going.
Let other traffic go first before you proceed.
Keep steady speed and watch for traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let other traffic go first before you proceed.
questions.explanation: A yield sign means slow down and be ready to stop if needed. Let any vehicle, bicyclist, or pedestrian pass before you go. You do not have the right-of-way.

questions.question: Why should you stay farther back when driving behind a large vehicle?

options.text: To see around the sides and see the road ahead.
Because other drivers pull behind large vehicles before passing.
Because following too close creates air pressure problems.

questions.correctAnswerText: To see around the sides and see the road ahead.
questions.explanation: Drivers of large vehicles cannot see you if you drive directly behind them. Stay farther back so you can see around the vehicle and see the road ahead.

questions.question: What does a single broken white centerline mean?

options.text: You must stay in your lane.
You can cross it to change lanes when safe.
You can only change lanes from the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can cross it to change lanes when safe.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. A broken white line means you can pass another vehicle when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: School crossing.
Pedestrian crossing.
Jogging trail.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrian crossing.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns you that pedestrians may cross the road here. Stay alert and let pedestrians cross safely.

questions.question: When driving on an interstate with traffic merging from on-ramps on your right, what should you do?

options.text: Change lanes to the left.
Slow down.
Maintain your speed and position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes to the left.
questions.explanation: When you see an on-ramp ahead, move to the left lane if traffic allows. This gives merging vehicles room to enter the interstate safely.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow centerline mean?

options.text: Passing is not permitted.
Passing on the right is permitted when the way ahead is clear.
Passing on the left is permitted when the way ahead is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing on the left is permitted when the way ahead is clear.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow centerline allows you to pass another vehicle on the left. You can only do this if the road ahead is clear and no traffic is coming toward you. Never cross a solid yellow centerline to pass.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Pedestrian crossing.
School crossing.
Jogging trail.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrian crossing.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert you to dangers ahead. This sign warns you that pedestrians may be crossing the road.

questions.question: When stopping on snow or ice, what should drivers with Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) do?

options.text: Pump the brakes.
Press and hold the brake pedal firmly.
Stay off the brakes and wait for the car to drift to a stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press and hold the brake pedal firmly.
questions.explanation: With ABS, press the brake pedal firmly and hold it. The ABS will pump the brakes automatically much faster than you could do it manually.
